newsitem.title: GERMANY: German online companies skimp on advertising-study.
newsitem.headline: German online companies skimp on advertising-study.

text.p: Despite mounting competition between online services in Germany, the industry spends relatively meagre amounts on advertising, media marketing company MediaGruppe Muenchen (MGM) said on Friday.

Online services only spent 7.6 million marks on advertising last year, MGM said basing its findings on a study it conducted. In comparison, cellular telephone companies spent about 319 million marks on ads or almost 42 times more.
"Online services spent less on advertising than was used to advertise batteries, for example," the MGM said.
"The development from a niche market to a mass market in this intensely competitive field requires that individual content advantages and convincing attributes be made known," the agency said.
MGM predicted by the year 2000 the number of cellular phone users and online-service users in Germany would each reach 14 million people, despite the gap between them in advertising.

Internet turnover could reach 1.2 billion marks by the year 2000, up from its current 300 million marks, and eventually represent a quarter of Europe's Internet income, MGM said, including online fees, software and services.

The three largest online services in Germany, T-Online, CompuServe and America Online had about two million subscribers at the start of 1997, MGM said. T-Online led the German market with 1.4 million users.
